Senses.Explanation: To turn oneself around is the bodily action of turning the body or self. It is attested 2,135 times in 327 allowlisted texts. The action can be direct narration: Magu Baoche turns intending to sit and is struck, while Sanfeng Hanyue Fazang turns and immediately walks away. Chan records also build a productive family from the same turning action. Yuanwu Keqin defines a “place to turn oneself” by “speak at the place without words; go at the place where going cannot be done” (無言處言得，行不得處行得，謂之轉身處). Hongzhi Zhengjue says one must know a road to turn; Yinyuan Longqi directly asks what that road is and answers, “you travel in the wild grass; I again enter the deep village” (汝行荒草裏，我又入深村). An unnamed questioner asks Poshan Haiming “what is a turning phrase?” (如何是轉身句) and receives a recorded answer. Feiyin Tongrong says that bright-eyed patch-robed monks have “no road to turn” (轉身無路), and elsewhere pairs turning with shifting step. Literal motion and the road, place, and phrase compounds preserve one turning action; the former targets were paraphrases, not different referents.
Senses.Note: Further collocations include “turn and shift step” (轉身移步), “no road to turn” (轉身無路), and “turn, then…” (轉身便). Later records use “turning phrase” (轉身句) as a label in stylized exchanges, while Zhongfeng criticizes stock phrases called by that name. Compare road to turn (轉身一路), turning phrase (轉身句), place to turn (轉身處), and shifting step (移步).

Occurrences.Kwic: 若向無言處言得。行不得處行得。謂之轉身處。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Blue Cliff Record of Chan Master Foguo Yuanwu (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄), spoken by Yuanwu Keqin. Yuanwu Keqin says: 'speak at the place without words; go at the place where going cannot be done—this is called a place to turn oneself.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 更須知有轉身一路始得。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Extensive Record of Chan Master Hongzhi (宏智禪師廣錄), spoken by Hongzhi Zhengjue. Hongzhi Zhengjue says one must further know that there is a road to turn oneself.

Occurrences.Kwic: 轉身移步若能行，荊棘林中活卓卓。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Feiyin (費隱禪師語錄): Feiyin Tongrong continues the same staff verse: if one can turn around and shift one's step, one stands vividly alive in the thorn forest.

Strict Lineage of the Five Lamps (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)), in the Linji Yixuan section: Mayu Baoche is the exact actor who turns, intending to sit; Linji Yixuan then strikes him. The following blow does not transfer the headword action to Linji.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Poshan (破山禪師語錄): an unnamed monk sets aside easy emergence inside the gate and difficult turning outside it, then asks Poshan Haiming what a turning phrase is. Occurrences.Kwic: 明眼衲僧轉身無路，現前大眾便合休機
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Feiyin (費隱禪師語錄): Feiyin Tongrong says in his teaching-seat address that the clear-eyed patchrobed monk has no road on which to turn around.

Recorded Sayings of Monk Sanfeng Cang (三峰藏和尚語錄): inside his Shengen Monastery exchange, Sanfeng Hanyue Fazang turns around and immediately walks away when pressed for another statement; the text then begins a new hall address.

Occurrences.Kwic: 更須知有轉身一路始得。如何是轉身一路？汝行荒草裏，我又入深村。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yinyuan (隱元禪師語錄), Yinyuan Longqi's Huangbo Mountain record. In his release-of-retreat hall address, Yinyuan Longqi says one must further know a road of turning around, asks what that road is, and supplies the paired line about walking through wild grass and entering the deep village.
